title: Printed bar model template
subject: Mathematics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y3 lessons 62, 63, 69 (Printed bar model template)
intro: To understand how to find a non-unit fraction of a set of objects

questions.q: 1/5 of a number is 6. Find it.
3/4 of a number is 12. Find it.
1/8 of a number is 4. Find it.
Sara runs 3/10 km then 4/10 km. Total?
A jug holds 1 litre. 3/5 is poured out. How much is left?
How much more is 7/9 than 2/9?
A class has 24 pupils. 5/8 have a sister. How many do not?
Which is more: 3/4 of 16 or 2/3 of 15? Show both bar models.
1/6 is 5; 2/3 is 10; 3/5 is 9. Find each whole.
Amina read 3/8 of her book: 24 pages. How many pages in the book?
True or false: if 1/4 is 9, then 3/4 is 27 and the whole is 36. Explain.
Omar paints 2/7 of a wall on Monday and 3/7 on Tuesday. How much is painted? How much is left?
questions.model: Teacher: add the days, then subtract from 7/7.

questions.q: A bag of rice: 4/12 used for lunch, 5/12 for dinner. What fraction is left?
Write your own two-step fraction problem with an answer of 1/5.
Big question: how does 1/5 help us find 3/5?
questions.a: Find 1/5 by dividing by 5, then multiply by 3

questions.q: 1/4 is 6. The whole? A) 24 B) 10 C) 2
Big question: can we find the whole from a part?
questions.a: Yes: find 1 part, then multiply by the denominator

questions.q: Big question: how do we know to add or subtract?
questions.a: Read the question: total means add; left or difference means subtract
